newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds finish up, eye on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds finish up, eye on U.S. data.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Monday as some slight buyer interest kept the market afloat ahead of anticipated direction-setting U.S. economic indicator releases later in the week.
"We have to see what happens with the figures" to get an idea of where the market is going, said a trader at a foreign bank.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/4 to 92-1/2, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was up $0.22 at 115.25.
Traders said there is a degree of caution ahead of the release of U.S. inflation figures later in the week and retail sales figures Tuesday.
Players worry that the figures could show climbing inflation which could push the Federal Reserve to raise rates more than expected May 20.
"Even though players have discounted for a rate hike, the market is cautious before the final result is known," said another trader.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 6.03 percent from 5.83 percent.
